name: Deductive Reasoning
definition: The ability to apply general rules to specific problems to produce answers that make sense.

benchmark.name: LogiQA
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on LogiQA test set, 4-way multiple choice
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: adults who take civil-service-style logical reasoning tests and do rule-application reasoning at work, such as college-educated applicants and professionals.

benchmark.name: LogiQA
benchmark.metric: accuracy (%) on the LogiQA test set, 4-option multiple choice
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: typical adults who take or do work comparable to Chinese civil-service logical-reasoning sections, such as administrative and analytical staff.

benchmark.name: FOLIO
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated adults who apply general rules to specific cases in their work, such as analysts, compliance staff and paralegals. They have no formal logic training.

benchmark.name: FOLIO
benchmark.model_or_system: GPT-4 (gpt-4) with Logic-LM (symbolic solver framework, without self-refinement)
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated adults who apply general rules to specific cases at work. These are not trained logicians.

benchmark.name: ZebraLogic
benchmark.metric: overall puzzle accuracy (%) on 1,000 puzzles; per-difficulty scores were 98.57% on easy and 60.83% on hard
benchmark.human_reference: General adult / educated workforce doing rule-based deductive problem solving (a typical adult solving logic-grid puzzles with pencil and paper, no solver tools)

benchmark.name: KOR-Bench
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated knowledge workers who routinely apply explicit rules or procedures to specific cases (analysts, compliance and QA staff, technical workers), working carefully under a single-attempt condition.

benchmark.name: BIG-Bench Extra Hard
benchmark.human_reference: Relevant educated workforce: college-educated professionals who do rule-based and analytical reasoning at work, such as analysts, auditors and technical staff.
